messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the solid–liquid equilibrium line on the water phase diagram lies below 0 °C.  
Using the standard phase‑diagram data for pure water, the melting/freezing temperature at 10 kPa is roughly **–2.8 °C** (about –5 °F).

> *Why this value?*  
> The freezing point of water drops as the external pressure falls because the liquid phase occupies more volume than ice. The phase diagram shows that at 10 kPa the solid–liquid coexistence line intersects the temperature axis near –2.8 °C.  

*(Note: The provided `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point` function only returns boiling points, so it cannot be used directly for freezing-point calculations.)*
